quitReasons: Fun drained steadily: office-sitcom filler like the pantry yoghurt, thin binary choices, and a few on-the-nose lines wore down my patience.
Nothing broke; three careers in, the beats felt familiar and I'd seen enough for a review. Fun just drained.
Cards settled into familiar formulas; the sharp lines stopped arriving often enough, and the institutional slips kept pulling me out.
Cards started repeating and the fun meter kept slipping; good callbacks were too sparse to outweigh the familiar career-sim beats.
Good callbacks kept me going, but the honesty-versus-comfort and work-life cards kept recurring in different clothes; I saw the template coming.
Too many familiar integrity tests and padded irony beats; the Chee Meng payoffs were great, but the rest turned formulaic and my interest ran out.
Fun ran out: too many quiet filler years and recycled thriller and recruiter beats, plus a couple of winks at the player.
Beats started repeating: stock work-life dilemmas, predictable options, and a fourth-wall gag. Few real surprises left to justify another career.
Tropes and fake choices piled up; the Director's wink at 'a game' broke the spell and I stopped caring.
Choices kept feeling pre-sorted and familiar, the Director winking at the phone broke the spell, and nothing surprised me enough to continue.
